title: Global Financial Crisis Tests Bahrain's Banking Sector
reason: Independent sources (MEED, IMF) confirm the 2008 global financial crisis exposed Bahrain's banking sector to real stress: Gulf International Bank and Arab Banking Corporation (both Manama-headquartered) reported combined losses of about $2bn for 2008 from subprime-related investments; the Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB) responded with regulatory tightening in 2008 (higher capital charges on real estate exposure, intensified bank inspections after the September 2008 Lehman collapse, monitoring of interbank exposure and liquidity) explicitly aimed at protecting Bahrain's reputation as a regional financial hub. The 'over 350 institutions' figure in the description is corroborated in magnitude — Bahrain was widely reported to host 400+ licensed financial institutions in this era (falling to ~134 by 2011 post-crisis consolidation), so 'over 350' is a reasonable characterization rather than a fabricated figure. Government/regulatory intervention (CBB taking control of two distressed banks, TIBC and Awal Bank) crystallized more fully in mid-2009, but the crisis onset, bank losses, and initial regulatory tightening are squarely 2008 events, matching the description. No off-limits domain (bis.org) was used as corroboration.
